title: To whom shall we go (John 6:60–69)
hookLine: many walk away; Peter says thou hast the words of eternal life

cards: It ends in a synagogue in Capernaum, where John says Jesus taught all of it: the bread, the flesh, the blood. And it costs him.
Not the hillside crowd this time: his own disciples, people who had been following him, start to leave. Some of them may have eaten the loaves by the lake. Jesus watches them go.
He doesn't run after them with a softer version. Then he turns to the twelve still standing there and asks a question that leaves the door wide open.

teach.b: It starts with a complaint, in the Douay-Rheims: "This saying is hard, and who can hear it?" Not just hard to understand. Hard to accept.
Jesus knows they're murmuring, and he doesn't take it back. His words, he says, are spirit and life, and some of them don't believe.

teach.h: MANY WALKED NO MORE WITH HIM.
teach.b: Then: "After this many of his disciples went back; and walked no more with him."
Jesus turns to the twelve: "Will you also go away?" Not a threat. A real question.
He lets them choose. And Peter answers, first and from the gut: "Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life." Notice what Peter doesn't say.
Not, I understand it all now. Not, it isn't hard. Not even, I'm sure.
Just: where else would we go?

teach.h: THOU HAST THE WORDS OF ETERNAL LIFE.
teach.b: It's the faith of someone who has looked at the alternatives and can't walk away from these words. Then he adds: we have believed and have known that thou art the Christ, the Son of God.

Some Catholics turn to this line on days when the teaching is hard, or the Church is hard to love, or God is silent. Staying isn't the same as having no questions. Peter will deny Jesus three times before the story ends.
But here, when it costs something, he stays.

how: Catholics hear Peter's answer on the Twenty-first Sunday in Ordinary Time in Year B, the last of the Sundays that read through John 6.

games.q: you're Peter. you've just watched many disciples walk away over a hard teaching, and Jesus asks if you'll go too. what do you say?
o: give me time to think about it.
Lord, to whom shall we go?
games.why: "Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life." he doesn't claim to understand. he stays.

practice: Think of something you're tempted to walk away from, a commitment, a friendship, a hard conversation, maybe even this path, and don't decide anything; just stay with it for now, noticing the urge to get up and go without following it.
If you pray, use Peter's words, Lord, to whom shall we go; if not, notice what staying feels like.
